extraction.name: Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval)
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating large language models on instruction following using prompts with verifiable instructions. It focuses on objectively checkable constraints such as word count, language, formatting, and other detectable properties.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was created by synthesizing prompts with verifiable instructions through few-shot prompting and manual curation, then manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts one by one. Model responses were collected via API calls.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Around 500 prompts (specifically 541 prompts) containing one or more verifiable instructions, plus the corresponding model responses used for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: GPT-4 responses were collected in November 2023 and PaLM 2 Small responses in August 2023.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports evaluation metrics for instruction-following accuracy, including strict and loose accuracy at prompt and instruction levels.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A few-shot prompting approach was used to identify illogical prompts and to rephrase prompts; verification was done with deterministic programmatic checks rather than human annotation tools.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes potential biases and inconsistencies in human evaluation, and that model-based evaluation depends on the correctness of the evaluator model, which can yield misleading signals if the evaluator has limitations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are fully verifiable objectively and automatically; edge cases can cause false negatives with naive verification. The current implementation can be improved by increasing the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions and extending to multimodal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper emphasizes safety and reliability of LLM instruction following, noting that misunderstandings can have dire results in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset/benchmark is intended for evaluating instruction-following ability of language models, with reported results used as baselines. The authors also release code and prompts for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the code and prompts are released, but it does not describe versioning, update timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policies.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The paper creates prompts through synthesis and manual curation, including generating base prompts with one to three verifiable instructions, removing illogical prompts, rephrasing prompts to increase diversity, and manually checking and editing them.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts were synthesized by appending verifiable instructions to base prompts, then filtering illogical prompts and manually editing rephrased prompts to make them diverse and suitable for evaluation.
